_strings.@@c084b10bf73d: Treaty conformity — PA does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by PA. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: PA does NOT start from federal adjusted gross income. Per the 2025 PA-40 instructions and the PA PIT Guide, PA imposes a flat 3.07% tax on eight SEPARATELY-computed classes of income (2025 PA-40 lines 1a-8: compensation; interest income; dividend and capital gains distributions income; net income or loss from the operation of a business, profession, or farm; net gain or loss from the sale, exchange, or disposition of property; net income or loss from rents, royalties, patents, or copyrights; estate or trust income; gambling and lottery winnings). PA provides no standard deduction or personal exemption ("PA law does not allow standard deductions, deductions for personal exemptions, itemized deductions, or deductions for personal expenses" — 2025 PA-40IN) and the 2025 instructions state PA filing requirements "are different than federal requirements." Because PA computes taxable compensation from gross PA-source wages rather than inheriting federal AGI, there is NO automatic federal-AGI pass-through that would carry a federal tax-treaty exclusion into the state return, and the 2025 PA-40 instructions contain zero occurrences of "treaty"/"treaties" (no treaty pass-through mechanism). Under the task rubric this is the state-builds-income-from-scratch (not federal AGI), no-treaty-pass-through case -> conforms_to_federal_treaties = false. CAVEAT: In administrative practice PA generally does not tax compensation a federal treaty exempts (such wages typically are excluded from PA-taxable Box 16 compensation), so the precise treatment of treaty-exempt income should be confirmed with the PA DOR; flagged in unverified.

warnings: Remote-work trap: work performed from TX for an employer sitting in PA, and PA HAS a convenience-of-the-employer sourcing rule. 61 Pa. Code § 109.8: "Any allowance claimed for days worked outside of this Commonwealth shall be based upon the performance of services which, of necessity, obligate the employe or casual employe to perform out-of-State duties in the service of his employer or casual employer." Out-of-state days reduce Pennsylvania-source compensation only when the employer's business NECESSITY — not the employee's convenience — puts the work out of state. Trigger: A nonresident allocating compensation from Pennsylvania-based employment between in-state and out-of-state working days. Exceptions: Days that of necessity obligate out-of-State duties in the employer's service qualify for the allowance; the regulation names no home-office factor test — necessity is the single standard. [61 Pa. Code § 109.8 (Compensation of nonresidents) — operative allowance sentence transcribed verbatim. — https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/Display/pacode?file=/secure/pacode/data/061/chapter109/s109.8.html] If the rule reaches these wages, a NONRESIDENT PA return is required that the physical footprint alone never shows.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: PA-40 Line 12 (PA Tax Liability) = Line 11 (Adjusted PA Taxable Income = Line 9 minus Line 10 other deductions) x 3.07 percent (0.0307). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: PA does NOT start from federal AGI: it taxes eight SEPARATELY-computed classes of income (2025 PA-40 Lines 1a-8 — compensation; interest income; dividend and capital gains distributions income; net income or loss from the operation of a business, profession, or farm; net gain or loss from the sale, exchange, or disposition of property; net income or loss from rents, royalties, patents, or copyrights; estate or trust income; gambling and lottery winnings). Line 9 adds ONLY the positive amounts — a loss in one class may never offset income in another class. "PA law does not allow standard deductions, deductions for personal exemptions, itemized deductions, or deductions for personal expenses" — calc.state_tax multiplies the supplied PA taxable-income base only (pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0). PA Tax Forgiveness (Schedule SP, PA-40 Line 21) and other low-income relief are OUTSIDE this flat-rate computation — check Schedule SP eligibility separately (2025 Eligibility Income Tables: unmarried base $6,500, married base $13,000, +$9,500 per dependent child, 100% down to 10%). UNCHANGED for 2025: the 3.07% flat rate, eight-class system, and no-deduction rule are identical to 2024. Local earned-income taxes (PA municipalities/school districts) are NOT modeled here.
